examples.text: Оказывается, их гидрокостюмы из хвалёного капрона, которые они так усердно клеили в Москве, пропускают воду. — Надо было их прорезинить. Капрон подвёл!

glosses: The flesh around the teeth.
To chew, especially of a toothless person or animal.
To deepen and enlarge the spaces between the teeth of (a worn saw), as with a gummer.
A viscous water-soluble carbohydrate exudate of certain plants that hardens when it becomes dry, or such a substance as a component of a plant exudate.
Any viscous or sticky substance resembling the true gum.

examples.text: […] becoomed wi' the gum o' the coal-hill […]

glosses: Chewing gum.
A single piece of chewing gum.

examples.text: Do you have a gum to spare?
Levi unwrapped a gum and put it in his mouth.

glosses: A gummi candy.
A hive made of a section of a hollow gum tree; hence, any roughly made hive.
A vessel or bin made from a hollow log.
A rubber overshoe.
A gum tree, any of various types of trees or an individual thereof.
To apply an adhesive or gum to; to make sticky by applying a sticky substance to.

examples.text: However, Albert said in his audiotape and in his speech that a lever designed to release the lifeboat's block and tackle was gummed up with red paint.

glosses: To stiffen with glue or gum.

examples.text: He frets like a gummed velvet.

glosses: To inelegantly attach into a sequence.

examples.text: It consists in gumming together long strips of words [that] have already been set in order by someone else, and making the results presentable by sheer humbug.

glosses: To impair the functioning of a thing or process.

examples.text: That cheap oil will gum up the engine valves.
The new editor can gum up your article with too many commas.

glosses: To coat with rubber or a similar material.
